# Original-error thermal readout for general sparse-H quadratizations

## Scope and advance beyond Lab004

Lab004 controlled chain defects and conditioned full-QUBO-ground mass. Here the
readout event is explicitly a MINIMUM-COST FEASIBLE ORIGINAL ERROR, including
states with excited compiler auxiliaries. The declared dynamics/readout model is
terminal Gibbs equilibrium. No schedule/runtime/initial-state assumption is
asserted to imply that equilibrium, and no real-QPU or finite-time quantum
annealing comparison follows. The new objective is original-error distribution
fidelity under this explicit readout model, not another chain-consistency bound.

The methods accept any sparse binary H, finite signed additive weights and a
feasible syndrome; no named code family, rank assumption, geometry or maximum
column degree is required. Bounded row degree is needed only for the inexpensive
ordinary-compiler entropy audit; balanced-factor formulas have no such bound.
Compilation does not solve decoding. Exact reference enumeration is kept separate.

## 1. Why auxiliary entropy matters

For a standard intermediate XOR factor

    M(x+y-p-2a)^2,

valid triples x xor y xor p=0 have auxiliary energies{0,4M}. Invalid triples have
{M,9M} for001 and{M,M} for the other three odd triples. Thus valid local triples
are thermally balanced, but invalid triples are not. In a check chain, different
invalid-prefix paths can end at the same original parity; summing them can give
different auxiliary partition factors for original inputs of equal parity.
Therefore conditioning on the original syndrome does NOT in general produce
exact cost Gibbs sampling, even though all zero-temperature minima are faithful.
This explains why full-QUBO-ground and minimum-cost-original-error events differ.

For fixed original row bits b, sum the auxiliary spins by a two-state prefix
transfer. A transition from previous parity v to prefix p, consuming current bit
x, has factor

    T_x(v,p)=sum_{a=0,1} exp[-t M(v+x-p-2a)^2].

The first prefix is fixed by the first original bit. Multiply transitions for
all intermediate stages, then final factor exp[-tM(v xor x xor s)]. This gives
A_r(b;t) exactly in O(row degree) work for a given row assignment. The original
error Gibbs marginal is

    P(e) proportional exp[-t w·e] product_r A_r(e[row r];t),

where t=beta*alpha for exact uniform physical rescaling. This includes ALL
compiler excited states. Enumerating e costs2^n and is reference-only; auditing
all row factors costs sum_r O(d_r 2^d_r), inexpensive on bounded-row-degree H.

## 2. A thermally balanced quadratic XOR gadget

Let G be the four even flips of a three-bit tuple. Define

    B_M(x,y,p,a_G) = (M/4) sum_{g in G}
       [(x xor g1)+(y xor g2)-(p xor g3)-2a_g]^2.

Every term is quadratic because XOR with a fixed bit is affine. The four hidden
variables are independent. Visible-visible couplings and visible fields cancel
under the even-flip group average. The actual intermediate interaction graph
is K_(3,4), with hidden fields and no visible-visible edge; unused structural
square-expansion edges are not embedded.

For a valid visible triple, every copy has a unique zero-energy hidden choice,
so B=0 has a unique hidden extension. For an invalid triple, every copy has
minimum square residual1, so its minimum total energy is M. For a valid triple
with any wrong hidden variable, that copy costs M. Hence every nonzero whole
factor costs at least M. The construction is faithful with the SAME global
M>sum|w| penalty as the ordinary compiler; no gain is attributed to a stronger
unnormalized parity gap.

The group acts transitively on each parity class. Relabeling independent hidden
copies under that action proves the hidden partition factor depends only on
visible parity at EVERY t, not just at zero temperature. Explicitly, with
r=exp(-tM), its valid/invalid factors are

    a=(1+r)^4,       b=8r(1+r^2).

For valid triples all four hidden excitations have energy M. For invalid triples
three hidden bits are free and one excitation costs2M, with base energy M.
Importantly, the invalid factor has an entropy8. Thermal balance is not free:
it can weaken effective parity suppression and adds three hidden bits per
intermediate gate. No novelty/priority claim is made for gauge symmetrization
or parity representation; the contribution is its rigorous integration and
resource-accounted evaluation in this decoding pipeline.

A degree-d>=2 check uses d-2 intermediate gadgets and the ordinary final parity
factor. Summing prefix/hidden variables gives two row factors(V,I), initialized
at(1,r) for the final factor, and updated d-2 times by

    (V,I) <- (aV+bI, aI+bV).

Equivalently, V/I is determined by the product of binary parity transmission
ratios. Since a-b=(1-r)^4>=0, V>=I and the effective soft-syndrome penalty
kappa_r=log(V/I)>=0. Degree-one rows have(V,I)=(1,r); empty feasible rows cost0.
The balanced original-error marginal is EXACTLY

    P_bal(e) proportional exp[-t w·e-sum_r kappa_r 1{(He)_r!=s_r}].

Conditioning on He=s therefore yields exactly exp(-t w·e) on the affine feasible
set, independent of row dependence, row order, column degree or syndrome values.
The possible degeneracy of minimum-cost errors is fully retained. In particular,
if g_F(t) is their probability in the intended feasible cost Gibbs law, then

    g_F'(t)=g_F(t)(<w·e>_feasible-C*)>=0.

This is an actual ORIGINAL-ERROR conditional decoding ordering. It differs from
Lab004's ordering of full-QUBO-ground mass. It still does not order unconditional
readout unless feasibility/chain-defect contributions are also controlled.

Compiler size: ordinary intermediates use one prefix plus one carry; balanced
intermediates use one prefix plus four hidden variables. Total variables are
n+2 sum_r(d_r-2)_+ versus n+5 sum_r(d_r-2)_+. Actual edges per intermediate are
6 versus12, with shared endpoint interactions/cancellations accounted in the
saved graph. Both construction times and output sizes are O(n+m+nnz(H)).

## 3. General-H syndrome repair and a probability bound

This subsection reuses the parent agent's independently developed verified
right-inverse implementation, saved in independent/penalty_bound.py and hashed
in source provenance. It is scientific collaboration, not a blind agent test.
Choose independent original rows R and columns B so H[R,B] is invertible.
Let Delta_j be column j of that inverse, lifted to original coordinates B.
Then H[R,:]Delta_j is the unit vector j and, because R spans the row space,
H Delta(v)=v for every residual v in imH, where
Delta(v)=xor_{j in R:v_j=1} Delta_j. This identity is checked exactly over GF(2).
Let L_j=sum_{i in Delta_j}|w_i|. For any error e, repair it to

    e*=e xor Delta(He xor s).

It is feasible and its cost increase is at most sum_{j:v_j=1} L_j. The mapping
(e*,v_R)↔e is bijective between the feasible affine space times2^rank(H)
residuals and all original errors. This does not require a decoding optimum.

For a soft-parity Gibbs law with nonnegative kappa_r, the weight ratio of e to
its repaired e* is at most

    exp[sum_{j in R:v_j=1}(t L_j-kappa_j)],

because nonbasis row penalties are nonnegative and can be discarded. Summing
the bijection gives the cheap original-syndrome certificate

    P(He=s) >= product_{j in R}[1+exp(t L_j-kappa_j)]^(-1).

The bound uses independent original rows, not fictitious independent detector
statistics. It remains valid with dependent rows and arbitrary signed weights.
For balanced compilation, kappas come from the closed recurrence above. The
calculation is O(rankH) after the GF2 repair witness; its usefulness is explicitly
measured rather than inferred from positivity.

## 4. Ordinary-compiler entropy envelope

For each nonempty row, compute min/max of logA over valid assignments and max
logA over invalid assignments. Let

    R_r=max_valid logA-min_valid logA,
    kappa_r=max_valid logA-max_invalid logA,      R=sum_r R_r.

Conditioned on the original syndrome, log auxiliary weight varies by at most R.
A positive likelihood multiplier whose log range is R changes an arbitrary base
probability law in TV by at most tanh(R/4). To prove it, bound the absolute
centered multiplier by its endpoint chord, then maximize over its mean; the
maximum occurs at the geometric mean of its two endpoint values and equals
(sqrt(b)-sqrt(a))/(sqrt(b)+sqrt(a)). Therefore the ordinary conditional feasible
original-error law is within delta_aux=tanh(R/4) of intended cost Gibbs.

For any e and its repaired e*, the auxiliary weight ratio is bounded by
exp[R-sum_r kappa_r v_r]. Dropping a negative nonbasis kappa adds the conservative
constant N=sum_{r notinR} max(0,-kappa_r). Excluding the zero residual before
summing yields

    Z/Z_feasible <= 1+exp(R+N)
       {product_{j in R}[1+exp(t L_j-kappa_j)]-1}.

Its reciprocal lower-bounds syndrome feasibility. It reduces to the balanced
product bound when R=N=0. Negative kappa or high entropy can make the certificate
inconclusive; this is reported, not hidden. Empty feasible rows are omitted.

## 5. From physical consistency to actual original-error readout

Both compilers are embedded on the same target with all reduction/chain
coefficients and signed coupling-group ranges charged. Reuse Lab004's physical
tree-repair certificate. Let epsilon_chain bound any broken branch. Conditioned
on consistency, the logical Gibbs law is exact up to the final rationally audited
coefficient perturbation. Compose distributions as follows: root decode to
original e, condition on He=s, then compare with intended feasible cost Gibbs.
The total variation is at most

    min(1, epsilon_chain+epsilon_syndrome+delta_aux+delta_rounding).

For balanced compilation delta_aux=0 identically. Also, minimum-cost feasible
ORIGINAL-ERROR readout probability is at least

    (1-epsilon_chain) P_feasible_lower max(0,g_F(t)-delta_aux),

again with the explicitly audited rounding correction. g_F may be expensive to
compute; the certificate exposes a monotone reference family rather than
pretending to solve decoding. On tractable original n, exact enumeration gives
g_F and the actual projected readout reference. The multiplicative bound is
preferred when additive TV is too weak for a rare optimum event.

Numerical comparisons hold target, coefficient ranges and declared beta fixed.
Extra hidden variables, qubits, search failures and evaluation costs remain
separate. A balanced conditional law can be scientifically exact yet perform
worse unconditionally because it weakens feasibility or uses smaller alpha.
No finite-time annealing ordering follows from these endpoint statements.

## 6. Precision and limitations

Authoritative compiler coefficients are exact rationals for finite binary64
input weights/penalty. Balanced algebra uses M/4 exactly. Actual physical
binary64 programs receive Lab004's rational range/repair/ground-state audits;
terminal law comparisons allow their nonconstant coefficient L1 perturbation.
Stable log transfers avoid cancellation/underflow. Ordinary row enumeration
returns inconclusive above degree20 in this implementation. Saved floating
exponentials are numerical evaluations of proved formulas; independent review
owns outward/interval checks where strict probability comparisons are claimed.

Repair-witness preprocessing uses bitset Gaussian elimination and does not
solve decoding. Its column basis is selected greedily by |w| as a linear-matroid
minimum-weight basis, but minimizing the worst repair-column load is not claimed.
The certificate can remain conservative or vacuous, particularly at small beta,
large n, dense right inverses or large auxiliary entropy. Resource failures of
minorminer are search failures unless a separate count obstruction is given.

"""Conductance limitation for a declared classical late-hold local-bath model."""
from pathlib import Path
import sys,json,math,time
import numpy as np
from models import compile_model
from evaluator import evaluate,json_program,get_groups
from lp_allocator import allocate_lp
from embedding import graph_from_witness,qubo_to_ising
LAB=Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1];OUT=LAB/'results'


def kernel_candidates(data,witness):
    B=set(witness['basis_columns']);R=witness['basis_rows'];deltas=[set(x) for x in witness['repair_columns']];result=[]
    for i in range(data['n']):
        if i in B:continue
        v={i}
        for row,delta in zip(R,deltas):
            if i in data['rows'][row]:v^=delta
        if not all(sum(j in v for j in row)%2==0 for row in data['rows']):raise AssertionError('not a kernel vector')
        cost=sum(abs(data['weights'][j]) for j in v)
        result.append({'original_variable':i,'kernel_support':sorted(v),'absolute_weight_cost':cost})
    return result


def certificate(data,witness,embedding,p,rounding_tv=1e-10):
    roots={int(i):q for i,q in p['roots'].items()};trees={int(i):[tuple(e) for e in es] for i,es in p['chain_trees'].items()}
    margins={(q,r):v for q,r,v in p['edge_margins']} if isinstance(p['edge_margins'],list) else p['edge_margins']
    N=p['physical_qubits'];beta=p['beta'];t=beta*p['scale'];epsilon=p['classical_break_bound'];entries=[]
    for kv in kernel_candidates(data,witness):
        i=kv['original_variable']
        if len(embedding[i])<=1:continue
        logical_min=math.exp(-float(np.logaddexp(0.,t*kv['absolute_weight_cost'])))
        lower=max(0.,logical_min-epsilon-rounding_tv)
        ep=-math.expm1(-sum(math.log1p(math.exp(-2*beta*margins[e])) for e in trees[i]))
        row={**kv,'branch_size':len(embedding[i]),'branch_defect_bound':ep,'logical_marginal_min':logical_min,
             'physical_marginal_min':lower,'root':roots[i]}
        if lower<=0:row['status']='inconclusive_variance'
        else:
            gap=min(1.,ep/(N*lower*(1-lower)));row.update({'status':'certified','gap_upper_per_attempt':gap,
              'mixing_time_lower_attempts_tv_quarter':math.log(2)/(-math.log1p(-gap)) if 0<gap<1 else (math.inf if gap==0 else 0.)})
            row['mixing_time_lower_sweeps_tv_quarter']=row['mixing_time_lower_attempts_tv_quarter']/N
        entries.append(row)
    finite=[e for e in entries if e['status']=='certified']
    strongest=max(finite,key=lambda e:e['mixing_time_lower_sweeps_tv_quarter']) if finite else None
    return {'status':'certified' if strongest else 'inconclusive','entries':entries,'strongest':strongest,
            'model':'random-scan single-site heat-bath at fixed beta, Gamma=0; one physical-site attempt per step',
            'interpretation':'worst-case mixing-time lower bound, not decoding-success ordering'}


def main():
    td=json.loads((OUT/'target.json').read_text());target=graph_from_witness(td['target']);groups=[[tuple(e) for e in g] for g in td['coupling_groups']]
    folder=OUT/'dynamics';folder.mkdir(exist_ok=True);rows=[];start=time.perf_counter()
    for path in sorted(OUT.glob('*_balanced.json')):
        r=json.loads(path.read_text())
        if r['status']!='ok':continue
        emb={int(i):c for i,c in r['selected']['embedding'].items()};m=r['model'];h,J,c=qubo_to_ising(m['linear'],m['quadratic'],m['offset']);curves=[]
        for beta in [10.,20.,40.,80.]:
            u=evaluate(h,J,c,target,emb,groups=groups,beta=beta);p=allocate_lp(h,J,c,target,emb,u,groups)
            if not p['feasible'] or p['scale']<u['scale']:p=u
            pw=json_program(p);cert=certificate(r['input'],r['repair_witness'],emb,pw)
            curves.append({'beta':beta,'program':pw,'certificate':cert})
            rows.append({'name':r['name'],'beta':beta,'status':cert['status'],'strongest':cert['strongest']})
        (folder/(r['name']+'.json')).write_text(json.dumps({'name':r['name'],'source_file':path.name,'curves':curves},indent=2)+'\n')
    (OUT/'dynamics_summary.json').write_text(json.dumps({'records':rows,'elapsed_seconds':time.perf_counter()-start},indent=2)+'\n')
    print('models',len(rows)//4,'certified',sum(r['status']=='certified' for r in rows))

    gap <= Q(S,S^c)/[p(1-p)] <= epsilon_branch/[N p(1-p)].

# Parent branch: a standard-initial-state short-forward-anneal comparison

This branch addresses the finite-forward-model gap explicitly. The result is a rigorous but generally VERY SHORT time interval, not practical-time or adiabatic superiority. It is separate from the terminal-Gibbs claims.

## 1. General measurement expansion

Let H(u)=-(1-u)sum_q X_q+u E(Z) on N physical spins, start in |+>^N, and evolve for total dimensionless duration T. Fix any computational-basis readout event F. Time ordering gives, at basis state z,

    Pr_T(z) = 2^-N [1+(T²/12)sum_q(E(z^q)-E(z))]+O(T^4).

One direct derivation writes D=-sum X and integrates the second Dyson coefficient: integrals DD=EE=1/8, DE=1/24 and ED=5/24. The amplitude's first-order term is imaginary. Combining its modulus square with the second-order term leaves the neighbor-energy difference above. Odd probability coefficients vanish because every Hamiltonian matrix is real and changing T to -T conjugates the solution. This is the full forward anneal, not an encoded-state pause.

## 2. Matched physical programs with amplified original objective

Consider two physical programs with identical nonobjective fields, all couplings, active spins, branches and root readout, differing only by

    E_1(z)-E_0(z) = (eta_1-eta_0)/2 sum_i w_i z_(root i) + constant,
    eta_1>eta_0.

Let F be original-error feasibility AND minimum original cost C*, counting ALL auxiliary/chain states whose original roots decode to such an error. At T=0 its mass is P0=g*/2^n. Terms outside original roots cancel, and every optimal error has sum_i w_i z_i=2C*-sum_i w_i. Hence

    [Pr_1(F)-Pr_0(F)]/P0
      = (eta_1-eta_0)(sum_i w_i-2C*) T²/12 + O(T^4).

All hidden-variable, chain and penalty effects cancel from this difference at second order. The statement is family-independent, includes ties, and uses the standard |+> initialization. It does NOT prove monotonicity at longer T or for arbitrary changes of embedding/couplings.

The parent repair-penalty method supplies a natural matched change: preserve the physical penalty scale k and all chain/contact coefficients, while raise objective eta from k/(W+1) toward k/(C+1). Hardware field limits and actual static fidelity must be audited again. Reusing fixed roots matters; independently rerooting can change the scored event. This is a programming improvement on a fixed embedding, not a qubit-count gain.

## 3. Cheap bound on C* without decoding

Parameterize the affine feasible set by ANY GF2 particular solution plus a kernel basis. This is linear algebra, not weighted decoding. For uniform feasible errors, group coordinates by their nonzero kernel characters. A coordinate with zero character is fixed. Let mu be the uniform feasible mean of w·e. If a group has character a and reference signs z_i^0, its contribution to variance is

    Var = (1/4)sum_(nonzero characters a)(sum_(i:character_i=a) w_i z_i^0)^2.

Different nonzero GF2 characters are orthogonal under the uniform kernel parameter. A cost upper bound is U=sum_fixed w_i e_i^0+sum_varying max(0,w_i). Bhatia-Davis follows directly from (C-C*)(U-C)>=0 and gives

    C* <= mu-Var/(U-mu), when U>mu.

If U=mu the cost is constant and C*=mu. Therefore D_lower=sum_i w_i-2[mu-Var/(U-mu)] is a cheap lower bound on the short-time advantage coefficient. Signed/zero weights and fixed coordinates are handled explicitly. If D_lower<=0, return inconclusive rather than assuming every feasible set has mean sumw/2. If every coordinate varies, mu=sumw/2 and nonzero variance gives a positive bound.

Kernel characters come from the saved right inverse plus nonbasis columns; no minimum-cost error is computed during evaluation. Costs are bitset linear algebra plus rational group sums, polynomial in input size and precision.

## 4. Explicit finite-T and floating-program bounds

Drop global energy offsets. Let Lambda=(N+sum|h|+sum|J|)/2. The row-sum matrix norm bounds the time-integrated Hamiltonian. Every amplitude Dyson coefficient is bounded by 2^(-N/2)Lambda^k/k!, so the probability coefficient at order k is bounded by 2^-N(2Lambda)^k/k!. Summing over F and retaining even terms gives a relative remainder

    R(T) <= cosh(2Lambda T)-1-(2Lambda T)^2/2
         <= (2Lambda T)^4 / [24(1-(2Lambda T)^2/30)],

for (2Lambda T)^2<30. The last bound is a positive geometric bound on the even Taylor tail, avoiding cancellation.

An amplified rational ideal field may need binary64 rounding. If its nonconstant coefficient L1 error is rho, an infinity-norm Duhamel bound from the uniform initial amplitudes gives event probability error at most

    P0 * T rho exp(2Lambda_max T)
       <= P0 * T rho/(1-2Lambda_max T),

for 2Lambda_max T<1. This relative bound avoids losing the rare-event factor P0. Consequently a strictly positive rational lower bound

    Delta_eta*D_lower*T²/12 - R_0(T)-R_1(T)
       - T*rho/(1-2Lambda_max*T) > 0

certifies the ACTUAL rounded amplified program's original-error success exceeds the baseline at that finite T. Lambda_max covers ideal and rounded programs. The computation does not need P0, C*, a state vector or a global spectral gap.

The resulting interval is expected to be extremely conservative and can be operationally negligible for large programs. Positive curvature or a tiny certified T is not evidence of a useful moderate-time decision rule. The numerical extension below tests wider times and retains reversals.

# General-H original-error readout and annealing relevance

## Outcome

This round derives an exact original-error thermal description, develops a cheap
syndrome/readout certificate, and identifies a rigorous local-dynamics obstruction.
Controlled ordinary-instance experiments show why a better endpoint model need
not improve finite-work annealing. Practical finite-time quantum comparison
remains open; the parent agent investigates separate coherent-forward results.

The principal new compiler has an auxiliary partition function depending only
on original parity. Conditioned on the syndrome, it samples the intended
feasible-error cost Gibbs law exactly, including all excited auxiliaries. On
23 matched sparse-H instances it uses about twice the physical qubits and gives
1.81 times the logical scale. At the declared beta20, its inexpensive readout
TV bound is at most.25 on16/23, versus8/23 for the ordinary compiler. Exact n16
references improve minimum-cost ORIGINAL-ERROR probability on8/8 inputs.

Finite-work CLASSICAL simulations reverse the observed compiler ordering:
with equal attempted-update budgets, mean n16 optimum success is.00757 for the
ordinary compiler and.00195 for the balanced compiler, while their terminal
logical-Gibbs references are.04352 and.12039. Both fail to approach equilibrium.
The balanced compiler's exact thermal law is a useful analytical control; these
results do not establish it as a practical replacement for the smaller compiler.

## Model, event and research conditions

The input is general sparse binary H, feasible syndrome s and finite signed
additive weights w. The scored error event is He=s and w·e=C*, with all tied
minima counted. No observable map or hidden true error enters construction or
scoring. A feasibility witness is saved with generated data for audit, but the
construction never uses its error values. Logical-observable correction success
and observable-class maximum likelihood are outside the measured event.

The endpoint model is Gibbs equilibrium for the programmed Ising Hamiltonian,
with beta in reciprocal programmed-energy units. Relative to the prompt's
Hamiltonian B/2 convention, beta=beta_physical B/2 at Gamma=0. No physical time,
bath, device temperature or freezeout point is asserted to produce equilibrium.
Source-level rational fidelity and physical hardware ranges remain separate
from thermal and dynamical claims.

The explicit dynamical extension is CLASSICAL random-scan single-site heat-bath
updating. A fixed-beta terminal hold supplies the mixing theorem. Finite-budget
forward simulations start from independent uniform physical spins and use
beta(u)=20u, Gamma=0 throughout, with midpoint schedule values per attempted
update. These simulations are not quantum dynamics and do not estimate QPU
performance. Parent coherent-forward investigations are separately owned and
reported in the root report and independent/ artifacts.

This is user-authorized continuing reference research, with inherited context
and parent scientific collaboration. It is not a clean autonomous model test,
SciCode2 calibration or acceptance evidence. Methods and all protocol changes
are preserved. Prior labs and the original problem/prompt remain unchanged.

## Exact thermal balancing and general-H fidelity

The full argument is in THEORY.md. The ordinary intermediate XOR factor is
M(x+y-p-2a)^2. Valid visible triples have hidden energies{0,4M}; invalid triples
have{M,9M} or{M,M}. Thus local validity is balanced, but summing invalid prefix
paths can bias equal-parity original-error inputs.

The balanced compiler sums four independent-hidden copies under all even flips
of(x,y,p), each at strength M/4. Visible-visible couplings/fields cancel and the
actual interaction graph is K3,4. A valid triple has one zero-energy extension;
any invalid triple or wrong valid-triple extension costs at least M. Degree-d
rows use d−2 intermediate gates plus a final two-bit parity factor. Variable
counts are n+2Σ(d−2)+ versus n+5Σ(d−2)+; physical routing is charged separately.

With t=beta alpha and r=exp(−tM), a balanced gate has valid factor
(1+r)^4 and invalid factor8r(1+r²). The latter includes an entropy factor8.
Summing prefixes gives two row factors(V,I), initialized at(1,r) and repeatedly
updated by(V,I)←(aV+bI,aI+bV). Hence the exact original-error marginal is

    P(e) proportional exp[−t w·e−Σ_r kappa_r 1{(He)_r≠s_r}],
    kappa_r=log(V_r/I_r)≥0.

Conditioned on He=s, all row factors are constant, so the original-error law is
exactly intended feasible cost Gibbs. Minimum-cost-error probability in that
conditional law increases with t, including degeneracy. This concerns original
errors rather than full-QUBO-ground readout. It is valid for dependent rows,
arbitrary column degrees, irregular matrices and all feasible syndromes.

Both main compilers use the SAME M=W+1, W=Σ|w|, and have minimum nonzero parity
penalty M. Ground-state fidelity follows by comparing infeasible penalties with
the total objective range. The parent-collaboration follow-up uses a stronger
repair argument and separately recomputes the coefficient gap for M=C+1.

No priority claim is made for parity symmetrization, Boltzmann hidden units or
chain-strength tuning. The scientific result is their proved, resource-accounted
integration into a general-H readout evaluation and its validated limitations.

## Cheap original-error evaluation

The parent's independently verified weighted GF2 right inverse supplies
independent original rows R and repair columns Delta_j with loads
L_j=Σ_{i in Delta_j}|w_i|. Every error repairs to a feasible error with cost
increase at mostΣ_j L_j v_j for residual basis bits v_j. The feasible-space/
residual map is bijective. For balanced soft-parity factors this proves

    P(He=s)≥Π_{j in R}[1+exp(t L_j−kappa_j)]^(−1).

For the ordinary compiler, exact local row transfers give the valid-sector log
factor range R_aux and conservative soft penalties. They yield a syndrome
feasibility lower bound and conditional feasible-law TV error at most
tanh(R_aux/4). Nonbasis negative penalties are explicitly retained as a worst-case
correction; the implementation does not drop them incorrectly.

Composing chain consistency, syndrome feasibility and auxiliary entropy gives
root-decoded TV distance from intended feasible cost Gibbs bounded by

    epsilon_chain+epsilon_syndrome+delta_aux+delta_rounding,

capped at one. This is a distribution-fidelity statement without a decoding
solve. It exposes a monotone intended cost-Gibbs family; it does not estimate
its unknown optimum probability cheaply. A multiplicative optimum lower bound
is also available once that reference probability is known or bounded.

Measured witness+row-envelope+bound cost is median.98ms for balanced models
(max3.02ms) and median3.84ms for ordinary models. The ordinary worst case is
343ms at row degree17, reflecting its O(Σ d2^d) local enumeration. It returns
inconclusive beyond degree20. Balanced formulas and post-witness evaluation
are linear in row/output size and do not have that exponential-degree audit.
These costs exclude physical embedding, which is charged below.

The ordinary conditional entropy bias at beta20 is already small on n16:
actual maximum TV is.000979 and its conservative certificate maximum is.00369.
Therefore entropy removal alone does not explain the larger observed endpoint
optimum gains. Logical scale and soft-syndrome suppression also change. At
beta10 the ordinary bias can be substantial; all temperature points are retained.

## Frozen ordinary-instance experiment

PROTOCOL.md precedes results. Four fully specified generators reused read-only
from Lab004 cover random degree-four checks, irregular hub checks, rewired bands,
and graph incidence augmented with hyperchecks and a dependent row. Original
sizes n16/32/64 and new seeds8807(development),9901(held-out) give24 input matrices
and48 compiler models. Neither code geometry nor one named code is required.

Both compilers use the SAME ideal Zephyr g6,t4 target,1248 sites, h[-4,4],J[-1,1]
and signed coupling-group range[-13,10]. These are illustrative declared bounds,
not a device export. All node/edge/group lists and versions are saved. Eight
identical minorminer seeds have5s timeout and2 tries. Selected cut/LP allocations
minimize qubits subject to their own first-uniform-candidate alpha floor and
requested.05 chain-defect budget. Coefficient allocation and actual fields,
couplings, offsets, branches, trees, margins and source graphs are saved.

Ordinary compilation fits24/24. Balanced fits23/24; mixed-hypergraph n64 seed8807
exhausts all eight heuristic searches. This is a search failure, not a proved
resource impossibility. Matched comparisons use the23 common successful inputs,
with the missing balanced case retained. Balanced physical-qubit ratio averages

resource tradeoff, not an embedding compactness improvement.

Selected mappings are reprogrammed at beta10/20/40/80. The following coverage
uses the original-error TV certificate, rather than mere positivity of a bound.

| beta | Ordinary TV≤.25 | Balanced TV≤.25 | Ordinary TV≤.10 | Balanced TV≤.10 |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|10|0/23|2/23|0/23|0/23|

Parent independently derived and checked a minimum-|w| basis repair condition

## Scope and advance beyond Lab004

Lab004 controlled chain defects and conditioned full-QUBO-ground mass. Here the
readout event is explicitly a MINIMUM-COST FEASIBLE ORIGINAL ERROR, including
states with excited compiler auxiliaries. The declared dynamics/readout model is
terminal Gibbs equilibrium. No schedule/runtime/initial-state assumption is
asserted to imply that equilibrium, and no real-QPU or finite-time quantum
annealing comparison follows. The new objective is original-error distribution
fidelity under this explicit readout model, not another chain-consistency bound.

The methods accept any sparse binary H, finite signed additive weights and a
feasible syndrome; no named code family, rank assumption, geometry or maximum
column degree is required. Bounded row degree is needed only for the inexpensive
ordinary-compiler entropy audit; balanced-factor formulas have no such bound.
Compilation does not solve decoding. Exact reference enumeration is kept separate.

## 1. Why auxiliary entropy matters

For a standard intermediate XOR factor

    M(x+y-p-2a)^2,

valid triples x xor y xor p=0 have auxiliary energies{0,4M}. Invalid triples have
{M,9M} for001 and{M,M} for the other three odd triples. Thus valid local triples
are thermally balanced, but invalid triples are not. In a check chain, different
invalid-prefix paths can end at the same original parity; summing them can give
different auxiliary partition factors for original inputs of equal parity.
Therefore conditioning on the original syndrome does NOT in general produce
exact cost Gibbs sampling, even though all zero-temperature minima are faithful.
This explains why full-QUBO-ground and minimum-cost-original-error events differ.

For fixed original row bits b, sum the auxiliary spins by a two-state prefix
transfer. A transition from previous parity v to prefix p, consuming current bit
x, has factor

    T_x(v,p)=sum_{a=0,1} exp[-t M(v+x-p-2a)^2].

The first prefix is fixed by the first original bit. Multiply transitions for
all intermediate stages, then final factor exp[-tM(v xor x xor s)]. This gives
A_r(b;t) exactly in O(row degree) work for a given row assignment. The original
error Gibbs marginal is

    P(e) proportional exp[-t w·e] product_r A_r(e[row r];t),

where t=beta*alpha for exact uniform physical rescaling. This includes ALL
compiler excited states. Enumerating e costs2^n and is reference-only; auditing
all row factors costs sum_r O(d_r 2^d_r), inexpensive on bounded-row-degree H.

Let G be the four even flips of a three-bit tuple. Define

    B_M(x,y,p,a_G) = (M/4) sum_{g in G}
       [(x xor g1)+(y xor g2)-(p xor g3)-2a_g]^2.

Every term is quadratic because XOR with a fixed bit is affine. The four hidden
variables are independent. Visible-visible couplings and visible fields cancel
under the even-flip group average. The actual intermediate interaction graph
is K_(3,4), with hidden fields and no visible-visible edge; unused structural
square-expansion edges are not embedded.

For a valid visible triple, every copy has a unique zero-energy hidden choice,
so B=0 has a unique hidden extension. For an invalid triple, every copy has
minimum square residual1, so its minimum total energy is M. For a valid triple
with any wrong hidden variable, that copy costs M. Hence every nonzero whole
factor costs at least M. The construction is faithful with the SAME global
M>sum|w| penalty as the ordinary compiler; no gain is attributed to a stronger
unnormalized parity gap.

The group acts transitively on each parity class. Relabeling independent hidden
copies under that action proves the hidden partition factor depends only on
visible parity at EVERY t, not just at zero temperature. Explicitly, with
r=exp(-tM), its valid/invalid factors are

    a=(1+r)^4,       b=8r(1+r^2).

For valid triples all four hidden excitations have energy M. For invalid triples
three hidden bits are free and one excitation costs2M, with base energy M.

it can weaken effective parity suppression and adds three hidden bits per
intermediate gate. No novelty/priority claim is made for gauge symmetrization

resource-accounted evaluation in this decoding pipeline.

Authoritative compiler coefficients are exact rationals for finite binary64

## 7. A limitation for late-hold local dynamics

Consider a DECLARED CLASSICAL model of a terminal Gamma=0 hold: random-scan
single-site heat-bath updates, selecting one of Nphysical sites uniformly per
attempt, at fixed beta. Its reversible stationary law is physical Gibbs.
This is not coherent quantum evolution and is not asserted to model a device's
bath. It tests the thermalization assumption needed by endpoint conclusions.

For any nonsingleton original-variable branch, let S be states with its root
spin+1 and let B be states where that branch breaks. Any root-flip transition
has at least one endpoint in B. Split directed S→S^c flow into transitions with
broken starts and transitions with consistent starts/broken ends. Reversibility
charges the latter to broken root− starts, disjoint from broken root+ starts.
Each state has at most1/N total root-update rate, so

    Q(S,S^c) <= P(B)/N.

The indicator test function in the Poincare variational formula gives

    gap <= Q(S,S^c)/[p(1-p)] <= epsilon_branch/[N p(1-p)].

No independence assumption is used. For the balanced compiler, choose a verified
kernel vector v with v_i=1. The map e→e xor v preserves every row parity, so all
soft-syndrome factors are unchanged. Its objective changes by at most

    logistic(-t L(v)) <= p_i <= logistic(t L(v)).

Physical root marginal differs by at most the global chain/rounding TV bound.
If a=logistic(-tL(v))-epsilon_chain-delta_rounding>0, then
p(1-p)>=a(1-a) and

    gap <= g_upper=epsilon_branch/[N a(1-a)].

The algorithm uses verified fundamental kernel vectors from the saved repair
basis, choosing the lowest absolute-weight support among those containing i;
it does not solve minimum-weight-codeword optimization. Singleton branches,
fixed bits and nonpositive a return inconclusive.

Random-scan heat-bath is an average of conditional-expectation projections and
has spectrum in[0,1]. For a nonconstant eigenfunction, worst-case TV after k steps
is at least(1/2)(1-gap)^k. Thus if0<g_upper<1, its worst-case mixing time toTV1/4
is at least log2/[-log(1-g_upper)] attempted updates, divided by N for sweeps.
These are LOWER bounds on worst-case mixing time, not lower bounds on decoding
failure or comparisons of actual spectral gaps. An upper gap bound getting
weaker does not prove improved mixing. Coherent or collective updates can evade

# Lab005: general-H readout and annealing relevance

This is supervised continuing research, not SciCode2 difficulty calibration.

decoder-free original-error readout evaluation, a local classical mixing

independent penalty and quantum-forward branches are described in `REPORT.md`.

and the frozen protocol files for timing of methodological choices. The balanced
compiler is an analytical control with about twice the physical qubits. Its
endpoint advantage does not establish practical finite-time performance.

## Environment and inherited sources

Python and exact package versions are in `requirements.txt` and
`results/research_environment.json`. The native sampler was built using:

```sh
clang++ -O3 -std=c++17 scripts/anneal.cpp -o scripts/anneal_backend
```

The saved binary is specific to Apple arm64; rebuild it on other platforms.

and Lab002's compiler/embedding utilities, without modifying prior labs. The

# Sparse quantum-forward readout moments for general H

## Scope and convention

Use exactly the full physical closed-system Hamiltonian K(u)=−(1−u)ΣX+uE(Z), u∈[0,1], total dimensionless duration T, and initial |+> on every physical spin. Computational bit b has z=2b−1. The readout is the declared original-variable roots; every other spin is unobserved, including other branch sites and reduction auxiliaries. E contains the actual programmed fields/couplings; its additive constant can be dropped. This is a quantum dynamical expansion, not a thermal model.

The coefficients below are exact algebraic results. Binary64 evaluation of them is a fast numerical implementation; it is not an interval proof. Their T^4 truncation has no useful moderate-time remainder certificate in this work. Parent FORWARD_THEORY.md gives a separate, conservative finite-time remainder for a different comparison.

## Linked expansion and local formula

Write ψ_z(u)=2^(−N/2)exp[iTN∫_0^u(1−v)dv+φ_z(u)]. The exact log-amplitude equation, on the analytic branch near T=0, is

    ∂u φ=−iTuE+iT(1−u)Σ_q(exp[Δ_qφ]−1),
    Δ_qf(z)=f(z^q)−f(z).

Let L=Σ_qΔ_q, B=Σ_q(Δ_qE)^2, C=Σ_qΔ_qE Δ_qLE, D=Σ_q(Δ_qE)^3. Expanding φ=ΣT^kφ_k gives

    φ1=−iE u²/2,
    φ2=LE(u³/6−u⁴/8),
    φ3=i[L²E(u⁴/24−7u⁵/120+u⁶/48)−B(u⁵/40−u⁶/48)].

The fourth derivative integrates

    φ4'=−(1−u)[L³E(u⁴/24−7u⁵/120+u⁶/48)
                         −LB(u⁵/40−u⁶/48)
                         −C(u⁵/12−u⁶/16)+D u⁶/48].

At u=1, real probability has only even powers, since changing T to−T complex conjugates the real-Hamiltonian evolution. Thus

    |ψ_z(1)|² / 2^(−N) = 1+q2(z)T²+[q4(z)+q2(z)²/2]T⁴+O(T⁶),
    q2=LE/12,
    q4=−L³E/1344+LB/2240+C/576−D/1344.

For pairwise E=Σh_q z_q+ΣJ_qr z_qz_r, q4 is a Walsh polynomial involving at most four spins within one physical star. The explicit star coefficients are implemented in forward_moments.expansion. Enumerating all stars costs O(N+|J|+Σ_q degree(q)^3), which is linear in physical program size for bounded-degree target hardware. The number of polynomial terms is of the same order. This is not exponential in physical Hilbert-space size.

fourth_order_checks.py independently obtains all time-polynomial Dyson coefficients of each small state amplitude by exact rational integration, then compares both probability coefficients on every basis state. It does not reuse the log-amplitude recursion. All24 arbitrary physical Ising models,278 total basis states, pass, including normalization through T^4.

## General-H affine averaging

For feasible H e=s, Gaussian elimination supplies e=e0+Vy over GF(2), with y uniform on the kernel parameters. An original root spin is z_i=(2e0_i−1)χ_{v_i}(y), where χ_a(y)=(−1)^(a·y). Each unobserved physical spin is an independent uniform character. A physical Walsh monomial therefore has a key (unobserved-spin mask, kernel character) and a sign. Group equal keys; the uniform-feasible expectation is exactly the coefficient at(0,0), and the expectation of the square is the sum of all grouped coefficients squared. No minimum-weight correction is computed.

Let a2=〈q2〉_F, a4=〈q4+q2²/2〉_F, μ=〈w·e〉_F. Then

    P_T(H e_out=s)=2^(−rank H)[1+a2T²+a4T⁴+O(T⁶)],
    E_T[w·e_out | H e_out=s]=μ+c2T²+c4T⁴+O(T⁶),
    c2=Cov_F(w·e,q2),
    c4=Cov_F(w·e,q4+q2²/2)−a2 c2.

The covariance with cost is evaluated by XOR shifts of grouped character keys. Additional cost is O(nP) hash operations for P polynomial groups, plus GF2 elimination; exact bitset operation cost depends on matrix dimensions. The implementation does not enumerate2^nullity feasible errors. Sparsity alone does not promise near-linear Gaussian elimination or a strong low-order prediction.

Consider two programs with identical active spins, roots, driver, couplers and nonobjective fields, and objective field change Δη w_i/2 at each original root. Their exact q2 difference is

    δq2=Δη[Σ_i w_i−2(w·e_out)]/12.

Consequently

Conditional optimum probability has relative T² coefficient improvement Δη(μ−C*)/6≥0. This latter identity contains the unknown optimum C*; the conditional-cost coefficient uses a variance computable by affine characters. Signed weights, zero weights, tied optima, dependent checks, irregular degrees and fixed coordinates are allowed. If Var_F(cost)>0 and Δη>0, analyticity implies strict conditional mean-cost improvement for sufficiently small positive T in the ideal exact coefficient model. If variance is zero the order is inconclusive. A conditional mean-cost improvement is not an unconditional original-optimum probability ordering.

In particular, a compiler whose original root fields contain only the objective has c2=−α Var_F(cost)/6, if parity interactions on root-only subsets are constant on F and all other factors average to zero. # A system-size-independent local-observable quantum remainder

This result applies to the same physical forward Hamiltonian and |+> initialization as QUANTUM_MOMENT_THEORY.md. It is separate from terminal equilibrium and the global original-optimum event. It gives a concrete finite-T guarantee for local observables, not just a formal Taylor coefficient.

Let O have support size s and operator norm at most1. At normalized time u, the sum of Hamiltonian-term norms incident on any one site is bounded by

    g(u)=1−u+u gE,
    gE=max_q(|h_q|+Σ_r|J_qr|).

Expand every nested Heisenberg commutator termwise over the one/two-site Hamiltonian terms. A nonzero next term must touch the current term's support; it adds at most one site. The incident-norm sum is at most(s+j)g(u) at step j, and ||[A,B]||≤2||A||||B||. Therefore the sum of norms of all order-k terms before time integration is at most

    2^k (s)_k Π_j g(u_j),
    (s)_k=s(s+1)...(s+k−1).

This argument tracks each nested LOCAL-TERM commutator, not the support of their sum. Internal-edge double counting is conservative. The scalar product Πg(u_j) is symmetric, so its ordered-simplex integral is (∫_0^1 g(u)du)^k/k!. With x=2|T|∫g=(1+gE)|T|, the absolute order-k expectation coefficient is bounded by(s)_k x^k/k!.

For real K(u), real initial density and real diagonal O, complex conjugation gives U(−T)=conj U(T), hence the real expectation is even in T. Its remainder after the exact T^4 coefficients is, for x<1, bounded by the positive even negative-binomial tail

    R_s(x)=[(1−x)^(−s)+(1+x)^(−s)]/2
                    −1−binom(s+1,2)x²−binom(s+3,4)x⁴.

For s=1, R_1=x^6/(1−x²). This bound depends on local incident strength, observable support and duration, not total physical spin count. It does not justify the same size-independent guarantee for a global feasible-optimum event.

Uniform physical-spin averaging extracts the single-root Walsh coefficient of q2 and q4+q2²/2, giving exact coefficients c2,c4 for E[C_out]. For two actual binary64 programs A,B, treated as exact rational coefficients, a lower bound on mean-cost improvement of B is

    (c2_A−c2_B)T²+(c4_A−c4_B)T⁴

Every spin is physical, including branch and auxiliary dynamics. No additional rounding correction is needed because the coefficient calculation uses Fraction(actual binary64) throughout. # Parent branch: a standard-initial-state short-forward-anneal comparison

This branch addresses the finite-forward-model gap explicitly. The result is a rigorous but generally VERY SHORT time interval, not practical-time or adiabatic superiority. It is separate from the terminal-Gibbs claims.

## 1. General measurement expansion

Let H(u)=-(1-u)sum_q X_q+u E(Z) on N physical spins, start in |+>^N, and evolve for total dimensionless duration T. Fix any computational-basis readout event F. Time ordering gives, at basis state z,

    Pr_T(z) = 2^-N [1+(T²/12)sum_q(E(z^q)-E(z))]+O(T^4).

One direct derivation writes D=-sum X and integrates the second Dyson coefficient: integrals DD=EE=1/8, DE=1/24 and ED=5/24. The amplitude's first-order term is imaginary. Combining its modulus square with the second-order term leaves the neighbor-energy difference above. Odd probability coefficients vanish because every Hamiltonian matrix is real and changing T to -T conjugates the solution. This is the full forward anneal, not an encoded-state pause.

## 2. Matched physical programs with amplified original objective

Consider two physical programs with identical nonobjective fields, all couplings, active spins, branches and root readout, differing only by

    E_1(z)-E_0(z) = (eta_1-eta_0)/2 sum_i w_i z_(root i) + constant,
    eta_1>eta_0.

Let F be original-error feasibility AND minimum original cost C*, counting ALL auxiliary/chain states whose original roots decode to such an error. At T=0 its mass is P0=g*/2^n. Terms outside original roots cancel, and every optimal error has sum_i w_i z_i=2C*-sum_i w_i. Hence

    [Pr_1(F)-Pr_0(F)]/P0
      = (eta_1-eta_0)(sum_i w_i-2C*) T²/12 + O(T^4).

All hidden-variable, chain and penalty effects cancel from this difference at second order. The statement is family-independent, includes ties, and uses the standard |+> initialization. It does NOT prove monotonicity at longer T or for arbitrary changes of embedding/couplings.

The parent repair-penalty method supplies a natural matched change: preserve the physical penalty scale k and all chain/contact coefficients, while raise objective eta from k/(W+1) toward k/(C+1). Hardware field limits and actual static fidelity must be audited again. Reusing fixed roots matters; independently rerooting can change the scored event. This is a programming improvement on a fixed embedding, not a qubit-count gain.

## 3. Cheap bound on C* without decoding

Parameterize the affine feasible set by ANY GF2 particular solution plus a kernel basis. This is linear algebra, not weighted decoding. For uniform feasible errors, group coordinates by their nonzero kernel characters. A coordinate with zero character is fixed. Let mu be the uniform feasible mean of w·e. If a group has character a and reference signs z_i^0, its contribution to variance is

    Var = (1/4)sum_(nonzero characters a)(sum_(i:character_i=a) w_i z_i^0)^2.

Different nonzero GF2 characters are orthogonal under the uniform kernel parameter. A cost upper bound is U=sum_fixed w_i e_i^0+sum_varying max(0,w_i). Bhatia-Davis follows directly from (C-C*)(U-C)>=0 and gives

    C* <= mu-Var/(U-mu), when U>mu.

If U=mu the cost is constant and C*=mu. Therefore D_lower=sum_i w_i-2[mu-Var/(U-mu)] is a cheap lower bound on the short-time advantage coefficient. Signed/zero weights and fixed coordinates are handled explicitly. If D_lower<=0, return inconclusive rather than assuming every feasible set has mean sumw/2. If every coordinate varies, mu=sumw/2 and nonzero variance gives a positive bound.

Kernel characters come from the saved right inverse plus nonbasis columns; no minimum-cost error is computed during evaluation. Costs are bitset linear algebra plus rational group sums, polynomial in input size and precision.

## 4. Explicit finite-T and floating-program bounds

Drop global energy offsets. Let Lambda=(N+sum|h|+sum|J|)/2. The row-sum matrix norm bounds the time-integrated Hamiltonian. Every amplitude Dyson coefficient is bounded by 2^(-N/2)Lambda^k/k!, so the probability coefficient at order k is bounded by 2^-N(2Lambda)^k/k!. Summing over F and retaining even terms gives a relative remainder

    R(T) <= cosh(2Lambda T)-1-(2Lambda T)^2/2
         <= (2Lambda T)^4 / [24(1-(2Lambda T)^2/30)],

for (2Lambda T)^2<30. The last bound is a positive geometric bound on the even Taylor tail, avoiding cancellation.

An amplified rational ideal field may need binary64 rounding. If its nonconstant coefficient L1 error is rho, an infinity-norm Duhamel bound from the uniform initial amplitudes gives event probability error at most

    P0 * T rho exp(2Lambda_max T)
       <= P0 * T rho/(1-2Lambda_max T),

for 2Lambda_max T<1. Here the perturbation ramps as u*deltaE, so its integrated row norm is T*rho/2; the factor2 in the probability difference cancels that half. A generic constant perturbation would require an extra factor2. This relative bound avoids losing the rare-event factor P0. Consequently a strictly positive rational lower bound

    Delta_eta*D_lower*T²/12 - R_0(T)-R_1(T)
       - T*rho/(1-2Lambda_max*T) > 0

certifies the ACTUAL rounded amplified program's original-error success exceeds the baseline at that finite T. Lambda_max covers ideal and rounded programs. The computation does not need P0, C*, a state vector or a global spectral gap.

The resulting interval is expected to be extremely conservative and can be operationally negligible for large programs. Positive curvature or a tiny certified T is not evidence of a useful moderate-time decision rule. The numerical extension below tests wider times and retains reversals.

# Relative original-error events in local finite-forward quantum dynamics

## Scope and outcome

This extension preserves the actual event F: the original roots decode to a
minimum-cost feasible error, counting all ties and allowing arbitrary compiler
auxiliary and branch excitations. It gives a rare-event-relative remainder for
ANY original-root event, then an inexpensive sufficient comparison for matched
objective amplification. It does not replace decoding success by expected cost.

The physical model remains K(u)=−(1−u)Σ_q X_q+uE(Z), u in [0,1], dimensionless
duration T, initial |+> on every active physical spin, and final computational
root readout. E has actual programmed one-site fields and pair couplers. Offsets
commute and are omitted. Arbitrary sparse binary H, dependent rows, finite signed
weights, feasible syndromes and tied optima are allowed. This is not a thermal
model, QPU estimate, adiabatic theorem or comparison between arbitrary mappings.

## 1. A uniform-diagonal norm that retains rare-event mass

Every operator on N physical spins has a unique displacement representation

    A = Σ_v f_v(Z) X^v,
    A[z,z xor v] = f_v(z).

Define the norm

    ||A||_U = Σ_v 2^(−N) Σ_z |f_v(z)|.

Triangle inequality follows componentwise. It is not asserted to be an operator
norm or invariant under arbitrary unitaries. The only properties needed are:

1. |<+|A|+>| ≤ ||A||_U, because X^v|+>=|+>.
2. Translations f(z)→f(z xor q) preserve its uniform L1 norm.
3. Multiplication by a diagonal Pauli character preserves that norm.

For a diagonal event projector P_F supported on n original roots,
||P_F||_U=P0=|F|/2^n. The ratio uses root patterns, not full physical ground states.
P0 is positive when a finite-cost feasible optimum exists; it need not be known
or computed by the evaluator.

For a single Hamiltonian Pauli term cP, each commutator obeys

    ||[cP,f(Z)X^v]||_U ≤ 2|c| E_uniform|f|.

For P=X_q this is the translated difference f(z xor q)−f(z). For diagonal
P=Z_a or Z_a Z_b, it is f(z)[P(z)−P(z xor v)]X^v. These elementary formulas prove
the bound directly, without an invalid multiplication/operator-norm argument.

## 2. Support-relative time-ordered remainder

Track EACH LOCAL-TERM BRANCH before summing. Initially f depends on the n roots
and v=0. A nonzero next local term must touch the current operator support; a
pair term adds at most one physical site. After j commutators its support is at
most n+j. Merging all terms first would destroy this support bound and is not
part of the proof.

Let gE=max_q(|h_q|+Σ_r|J_qr|), and g(u)=1−u+u gE. Summing incident Pauli-term
norms over a support S is at most |S|g(u); internal-edge double counting is
conservative. Hence the norm sum of order-k nested terms is at most

    P0 2^k (n)_k Π_j g(u_j),
    (n)_k=n(n+1)...(n+k−1).

The ordered-simplex integral of the positive symmetric scalar product is
(∫g)^k/k!. Therefore the absolute kth coefficient of Pr_T(F)/P0 is at most

    binom(n+k−1,k) (1+gE)^k.

For real K, real |+><+| and real diagonal P_F, U(−T)=conj U(T), so Pr_T(F) is
even. This remains true under time ordering; conjugation reverses no product.
For x=(1+gE)|T|<1, the relative remainder after T² is bounded by

    R_n,2(x)=[(1−x)^(−n)+(1+x)^(−n)]/2
                 −1−binom(n+1,2)x².

The denominator P0 cancels exactly. An operator-norm observable bound divided by
P0 would lose this property and be useless for rare decoding events. The present
bound depends on original readout support n rather than total N, but it is still
not size independent.

## 3. Sharper driver/diagonal word counts

The special form of K yields stronger low-order majorants. In a local-term
branch after d driver and m diagonal-energy commutators:

- |v|≤d, because only a driver term changes the flip displacement.
- f depends on at most n+m sites. A nonzero diagonal pair term touches v, hence
  an existing support site, and adds at most one new dependence site.
- A driver commutator is nonzero only where f depends on that site. Its total
  norm multiplier is at most 2(n+m)(1−u).
- A diagonal commutator only uses terms incident on v, so its multiplier is at
  most 2d gE u, rather than the whole functional support.

These are termwise counts, not support claims for a sum. Let B[d,m](u) majorize
the norm of all inner-later words at times in [u,1], divided by P0. Set B[0,0]=1
and out-of-range indices zero. Then

    B[d,m](u)=∫_u^1 {
       2(n+m)(1−v) B[d−1,m](v)
       +2d gE v B[d,m−1](v)} dv.

In the Heisenberg Dyson series, the inner Hamiltonians are later in time and
outer ones earlier. Thus the [u,1] orientation is essential. All integrands have
nonnegative scalar majorants. The implementation factors out gE^m and integrates
exact rational polynomials.

Any outermost driver commutator has zero |+> expectation, since each X_q has |+>
as an eigenstate. Only words with an outer diagonal term need remain. Their
relative kth expectation coefficient is bounded by

    C_k(n,gE)=Σ_{d+m=k,m≥1} ∫_0^1 2d gE u B[d,m−1](u) du.

The first inner term must be a driver; the factor d already makes the all-E
words zero. In particular,

    C_2 = n gE/6,
    C_4 = n³ gE/56 + n(35n+17)gE²/1260 + n gE³/168.

For comparison, the generic fourth-order bound scales as n^4(1+gE)^4. The mixed
word bound retains the distinction between energy and driver insertions.
It does not exploit every cancellation or connected-cluster identity.

Fix K=12 before evaluating outcomes. The refined relative remainder is

    R_word(T) = Σ_{k=4,6,...,12}
        min[C_k T^k, binom(n+k−1,k)x^k]
       +{[(1−x)^(−n)+(1+x)^(−n)]/2
           −Σ_{k=0,2,...,12} binom(n+k−1,k)x^k}.

All coefficients inside the final braces are nonnegative. Exact rational
arithmetic avoids subtractive rounding in this tail. Higher orders use the
proved generic bound; no unproved mixed-word infinite-series convergence is
assumed. The two-program remainder is the sum of their separate remainders.

## 4. Actual rounded objective-amplification comparison

The matched programs have identical active sites, roots, driver, couplers and
nonobjective fields. Their actual root-field difference is

    delta h_i = Δη w_i/2 + epsilon_i,
    Δη>0, rho=Σ_i|epsilon_i|,

all interpreted as exact rationals for the saved binary64 values. The known
second-order density coefficient is q2=LE/12, L=Σ_q[f(z^q)−f(z)]. Consequently,
for the original optimum event,

    delta a2 = Δη(Σ_i w_i−2C*)/12
                    −Σ_i epsilon_i E[Z_i|F]/6
             ≥ Δη D_lower/12−rho/6 = A_actual.

D_lower≤Σw−2C* is obtained from the parent's exact affine mean/variance bound
without solving weighted decoding: C*≤mu−Var/(U−mu), with the constant-cost case
handled separately. This extension reuses that proved input and does not claim
its discovery. All tied optima have the same C*, so their uniform mixture obeys
the same bound.

Unlike a generic Duhamel rounding estimate, rounding here is charged directly
to the exact T² coefficient. All higher coefficients are already bounded for
ACTUAL rounded programs, and their odd coefficients remain zero. No separate
linear-in-T rounding penalty is necessary.

Thus

    [Pr_new(F)−Pr_base(F)]/P0
       ≥ A_actual T²−R_base(T)−R_new(T).

A positive exact rational right side certifies strict actual original-error
optimum probability improvement at that finite duration. The event, P0, C* and
optimal error patterns are never enumerated by the certificate. If A_actual≤0
or the remainder dominates, return inconclusive. A positive guarantee is not
universal over all H/s/w; e.g. forced costly feasible bits can oppose the short
forward bias. Static ground-fidelity and hardware-range audits remain separate
prerequisites for using the programs as decoding implementations.

## 5. Costs and limits

For fixed K=12, scalar polynomial majorants depend only on n and are cached;
program-specific work computes actual local strengths and evaluates exact
rational inequalities on a dyadic menu. There is no Hilbert-space or 2^nullity
enumeration. Bit lengths and rational arithmetic costs are charged; constants
in exact output fractions can be large. Hexadecimal numerator/denominator
strings make the saved exact witnesses portable across JSON integer limits.

This improves conservative finite-time ORIGINAL-OPTIMUM guarantees, rather than
only local mean-cost guarantees. It still covers very early evolution, says
nothing about moderate-time interference or practical annealing success, and
retains system-size dependence through n. An increased certified duration is
not an increased absolute success probability claim: P0 itself can be tiny.
EOF","max_output_tokens":1000}));

# Necessary-optimality bounds without an optimum oracle

The physical/event model is unchanged from the parent's certified mapping study:
standard-|+> initialization, K(u)=−(1−u)ΣX+uE(Z), final original-root readout, and
the event of a minimum-cost feasible ORIGINAL error (all ties; arbitrary compiler
and chain excitations). This extension only improves the lower bound on the
actual second-order event coefficient. It does not replace the event by cost.

## General feasible characters

For arbitrary binary H and feasible s, exact GF2 elimination gives

    e(y)=e0 xor Vy,    y in GF2^k.

Write each original spin as Z_i=(2e0_i−1)χ_{a_i}(y), where
χ_a(y)=(−1)^(a·y). Thus the original cost is

    C(y)=mu+Σ_{a≠0} c_a χ_a(y).

Fixed coordinates and signed/zero weights are included in mu and c. Let U* be
ANY proved upper bound on the unknown minimum C*: the parent's affine-moment
bound, the exact cost of e0, or the cost of a verified feasible witness. No
claim that a feasible witness is optimal is necessary or permitted.

For any two actual physical programs read to the same original variables,
uniform nonroot averaging gives the exact second-order difference polynomial

    f(y)=delta q2_F(y)=a0+Σ_{a≠0} a_a χ_a(y).

The root-only coefficients are extracted directly from actual binary64 fields
and root-root couplers as exact Fractions: −h_i Z_i/6 and −J_ij Z_i Z_j/3.
Unobserved branch/auxiliary terms average to zero at this order. Root labels,
branch sizes and total physical spin counts may differ. The final event's
initial mass P0 depends only on original optimal patterns and is the same.

## Necessary optimality inequalities

For any selected nonzero parameter move t, a global optimum obeys
C(y xor t)−C(y)≥0. Character multiplication therefore proves

    Σ_{a:a·t=1} c_a χ_a(y)≤0.

The implementation includes fundamental moves t=unit_j, then all parameter
pairs unit_i xor unit_j. These are polynomially many necessary conditions,
not a global optimization oracle. They apply to every tied optimum, even if a
separate feasible witness is not locally optimal or hits its search cap.

For any nonzero a,b,c=a xor b, characters obey χ_c=χ_aχ_b. The convex hull of
(χ_a,χ_b,χ_c) is described by the four valid inequalities

    −x_a−x_b−x_c≤1,
    −x_a+x_b+x_c≤1,
     x_a−x_b+x_c≤1,
     x_a+x_b−x_c≤1.

Only triples induced by original-coordinate character pairs whose XOR is already
present are included. There is no exponential character closure or claim that
these facets describe all feasible character vectors.

Together with Σc_a x_a≤U*−mu and −1≤x_a≤1, these inequalities define a relaxation
containing every unknown optimal error character vector and any mixture of ties.

## Exact dual lower certificate

Collect the selected necessary inequalities as A x≤b. For ANY nonnegative
multipliers nu, and every actual optimum,

    f(y)≥a0−nu·b−Σ_a |a_a+(nu^T A)_a| = L2(nu).

Indeed f+nu·(Ax−b)≤f, and minimizing the left expression over the box gives the
formula. This proof does not require the numerical LP to be optimal, its primal
solution to be feasible, or any near-zero residual to be ignored.

HiGHS proposes multipliers from the numerical LP's inequality marginals.
Nonnegative binary64 multipliers are converted to exact rational values; negative
proposals are clipped to zero. All remaining coefficients are charged in the
exact L1 box minimum. The saved witness identifies every nonzero multiplier by
constraint ID. Earlier valid bounds are retained by taking their maximum, so a
weak numerical proposal never invalidates a previously proved lower bound.

The parent's one-dimensional cost-only Lagrange bound is a special case. Exact
breakpoint maximization of it is retained as a mechanism control under both
improved upper witnesses.

## Composition with the actual event certificate

The parent's exact physical fourth-order polynomial supplies a pointwise
feasible lower bound L4. The proved relative word-majorant tails bound the
remainder beyond T4 separately for both programs. Hence

    [P_candidate(opt)−P_first(opt)]/P0
      ≥ L2 T²+L4 T⁴−R_candidate,>4−R_first,>4.

The extension reuses the parent's EXACT stored lower gaps and updates them by
(L2_new−L2_old)T². This changes no fourth coefficient, physical program, event,
duration, tail or resource condition. All ordinary decisions use exact rational
positivity. Candidate selection is smallest N≤FIRST among strict certificates,
then greatest exact proved lower gap, then original seed; fallback FIRST.

For an upper bound on actual second-order difference, apply the same relaxation
to −f and negate its lower bound. A nonnegative upper bound is inconclusive.
No adverse actual ordering was proved in this study.

## Feasible witnesses and computational scope

The zero-search witness is the already computed affine particular solution e0.
Its original error is directly checked against H/s and its cost summed exactly.
The searched witness uses 16 fixed feasible kernel starts, then best-improving
fundamental/pair kernel descent, capped at4n accepted moves per start. Every move
stays feasible. The best visited error is a valid cost upper witness regardless
of local termination; it is not asserted optimal. No ordinary reference optimum
or planted generator error is consulted.

The implementation forms exact Fraction values of finite signed binary64 weights
and scales them by the LCM of their denominators. This supports arbitrary finite
binary64 weights, not only quarters. Measured instances have small dyadic
weights; large denominator/numerator bit lengths can substantially increase
integer/rational work. Arbitrary-real exact weights and arbitrary-precision
input formats are not claimed by the JSON interface. LP proposals use floating
arithmetic, but the returned bound is checked algebraically in exact arithmetic.

Basis/pair move enumeration and selected triangle construction are polynomial;
GF2 preprocessing, numerical LP cost and exact bit complexity are not promised
linear in general H. The ordinary suite measures n16/32/64 and bounded target
hardware. Only the small validation suite enumerates optima, explicitly separated
from ordinary construction/selection.
